name: Hermes Agent (w/ Dashboard)
description: Hermes AI agent for Telegram, Discord and Slack, with a password-locked web dashboard

upstream.$note: Upstream publishes an official image on Docker Hub (revision 345cd2b = tag v2026.9.14), so nothing is built from source. The incumbent 2691-deploy template clones the repo and compiles the React dashboard at build time, which is a multi-minute build with a documented trail of pyproject pin traps (nemo-relay floors, uv exclude-newer, editable-install-only). None of that applies here.

positioning.$note: Marketplace is SATURATED for 'hermes': hermes-railway-template 4813 deploys (thin worker, no web UI), hermes-agent-ai 2691 (fat custom Starlette admin over a source build), hermes-agent-nous-research 1065, hermes 201. The gap is the intersection: the official image's own supervised dashboard, exposed and authed, with no custom server code. Name follows the one latecomer pattern that beats incumbents (N8N (w/ workers)): app name first, one capability qualifier in parentheses.

topology.$note: Single service, single volume. The official image is s6-overlay based: /init is PID 1, the container CMD runs as the main program (dies -> container dies -> Railway restarts), and the dashboard runs beside it as a supervised s6 longrun that s6 restarts on crash. That is upstream's own supervision, not ours. No Postgres: hermes keeps state in SQLite under HERMES_HOME.

hermes.startCommandNote: Deliberately unset. Railway execs a start command raw and discards the image ENTRYPOINT, which would bypass entrypoint-dispatch.sh -> /init and kill the whole s6 supervision tree (no dashboard, no cont-init bootstrap, no UID remap). The Dockerfile's CMD carries the gateway invocation instead.
hermes.healthcheckNote: Unauthenticated requests get a 302 to /login, which Railway counts as healthy, so no unauthenticated health route has to be exposed. Boot to first response measured at roughly 60s locally, inside the published-template 300s healthcheck ceiling.

volume.$note: The image's own HERMES_HOME / VOLUME / HERMES_WRITE_SAFE_ROOT are all /opt/data, so mounting there needs zero env overrides and inherits stage2-hook.sh's boot-time chown of HERMES_HOME plus its top-level state-file ownership sweep. Relocating to /data (as the 4813-deploy template does) costs four env overrides and a hand-written chown -R hook. Holds config.yaml, .env, sessions, state.db, memories, skills, pairing.

variables.HERMES_DASHBOARD_note: Baked into the Dockerfile too; the s6 dashboard service exits 0 and marks itself permanently down unless this is truthy.
variables.HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD_not: Required, not optional: the dashboard's auth gate fails start_server closed on a non-loopback bind with no auth provider, so a deployer who clears this gets no dashboard at all rather than an open one. secret(32) survives templateGenerate because it is a generator reference. Despite the name this is not HTTP Basic: anonymous requests 302 to /login and credentials post to /auth/password-login, which sets hermes_session_* cookies.
variables.HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_SECRET_note: Signing key for those session cookies. Unset, hermes mints a random key per process, so every dashboard restart silently logs everyone out. Pinning it to a per-deployment generated secret keeps sessions alive across restarts and redeploys.
variables.HERMES_DASHBOARD_PUBLIC_URL_note: Feeds should_require_dashboard_auth() and the MCP OAuth redirect_uri. Safe here because it always arrives alongside the basic-auth pair.
variables.TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS: prompted, optional, comma separated numeric ids

hermes.credentialsNote: No .env file is written at boot. hermes_cli/env_loader.py loads $HERMES_HOME/.env over os.environ but its startup scrub list (_PROFILE_MANAGED_ENV_KEYS) covers only ACP/Copilot routing keys and explicitly excludes credentials, so plain Railway variables reach the gateway unmodified.

verification.journey: Deploy -> open domain -> browser basic-auth prompt -> log in as admin -> Hermes dashboard loads (Chat, Keys, Skills) -> message the Telegram bot -> approve the pairing request -> agent replies
verification.contractTests: test/contract.sh: 401 anonymous, 200 authenticated, 401 on wrong password, v4-mapped connect to the v6 listener, gateway process alive, stale gateway.pid cleared across a container restart
